cities.tagline: A Mecklenburg County town with a walkable downtown and easy I-485 access
overview: Matthews is a town in southeastern Mecklenburg County, bordering Charlotte, with a population of 29,435 at the 2020 census. Its compact downtown along Trade Street and John Street anchors community life with local shops and restaurants.

Housing ranges from older homes near downtown to subdivisions built from the 1980s onward and newer townhomes. Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park and the Four Mile Creek Greenway offer outdoor space. Independence Boulevard (US 74) and I-485 connect Matthews with Charlotte, Mint Hill, and Union County. Most of the town uses ZIP code 28105, and some Matthews mailing addresses (28104/28105) actually lie in Union County, so buyers should verify the jurisdiction and county on each listing.
dining: Downtown Matthews restaurants (Trade St and John St)
shopping: Shopping centers along US 74 and NC 51

faq.q: What county is Matthews in?
faq.a: Matthews is in Mecklenburg County, although some homes with Matthews mailing addresses are in Union County.

faq.q: What ZIP code is Matthews?
faq.a: The town is mainly in ZIP code 28105; 28104 addresses are typically in Union County.

faq.q: Is Matthews near the light rail?
faq.a: No. Matthews is not served by LYNX rail; US 74 and I-485 are the main routes.

cities.tagline: A suburban town on Charlotte's southeast edge with room to spread out
overview: Mint Hill is a suburban town on Charlotte's southeast edge, mostly in Mecklenburg County with a small portion in Union County. Its population was 26,450 at the 2020 census, up from 22,722 in 2010. The town is close to the Cabarrus County line and has its own town government.

Housing is mainly single-family, from older homes on larger lots to newer subdivisions, with some townhomes and remaining acreage in the outer areas. Residents use I-485, Albemarle Road (NC 24/27), and Lawyers Road to reach Charlotte, and Matthews' shopping is a short drive south. Reedy Creek Nature Preserve and McAlpine Creek Park are nearby. Because Mint Hill is a separate municipality, property taxes include both county and town rates; homes in the Union County portion use Union County services, so verify the county on each listing.
dining: Restaurants along Matthews-Mint Hill Rd and Lawyers Rd
shopping: Shopping centers along Matthews-Mint Hill Rd

faq.q: What county is Mint Hill in?
faq.a: Mostly Mecklenburg County, with a small portion in Union County.

faq.q: What ZIP code is Mint Hill?
faq.a: Mint Hill mainly uses ZIP code 28227.

faq.q: Is Mint Hill part of Charlotte?
faq.a: No. Mint Hill is its own incorporated town.

cities.tagline: A small south Mecklenburg town with big retail and quick access to the state line
overview: Pineville is a small town at the southern tip of Mecklenburg County, between Charlotte and Fort Mill, South Carolina. Its population was 10,602 at the 2020 census, up from 7,479 in 2010. The town has a small historic downtown along Main Street and is best known regionally for Carolina Place mall and the retail corridors around it.

Housing includes older single-family homes near downtown, townhomes, and a large number of apartment communities. The LYNX Blue Line's southern terminus, I-485/South Boulevard station, is just north of town in Charlotte, and I-485, I-77, NC 51, and US 521 provide driving routes. Carowinds and the South Carolina line are minutes away. Pineville is a separate municipality with its own town services and tax rate, and many homes outside town limits also use the 28134 ZIP, so check jurisdiction carefully.
shopping: Retail along NC 51 and South Blvd
transportation: LYNX Blue Line – I-485/South Blvd station (nearby)

faq.q: What ZIP code is Pineville?
faq.a: Pineville uses ZIP code 28134, which also covers some areas outside town limits.

faq.q: Is Pineville near the light rail?
faq.a: Yes. The LYNX Blue Line's I-485/South Boulevard station is just north of town.

faq.q: What shopping is in Pineville?
faq.a: Carolina Place mall and the surrounding retail corridors.

cities.tagline: North Mecklenburg's largest town, between Charlotte and Lake Norman
overview: Huntersville is a suburban town in northern Mecklenburg County, about 14 miles north of Charlotte. With a 2020 census population of 61,376, it is one of the larger municipalities in North Carolina. The town stretches from the Charlotte line toward Lake Norman and Mountain Island Lake.

Housing includes master-planned communities, golf neighborhoods, townhomes, and some lakefront and lake-access homes. Birkdale Village is a popular open-air shopping and dining center, and Latta Nature Preserve offers trails, horseback riding, and Mountain Island Lake access. I-77 and I-485 are the main commuting routes, along with NC 73 and NC 115. Huntersville uses ZIP code 28078, and buyers should check whether a home is inside town limits or in unincorporated Mecklenburg County.

Housing ranges from waterfront estates and lake-access communities to golf neighborhoods, townhomes, and condos. Jetton Park offers walking trails and lake views, and the town's small historic downtown sits along Catawba Avenue. I-77 provides access to Charlotte to the south and Mooresville to the north, and NC 73 and US 21 serve local trips. Cornelius uses ZIP code 28031. Waterfront buyers should verify dock permits and Duke Energy shoreline rules, which govern docks and shoreline changes on Lake Norman.

overview: Davidson is a small town in Mecklenburg and Iredell counties, founded in 1837 with the establishment of Davidson College, a private liberal arts college. Housing includes historic homes near downtown, traditional neighborhood developments with sidewalks and parks, townhomes, and some lake-access properties. I-77, NC 73, and NC 115 connect residents to Charlotte and Lake Norman. Davidson uses ZIP code 28036, and buyers should check whether a property is in town limits and which county it is in.

overview: Belmont is a small suburban city in Gaston County, about 9 miles east of Gastonia and just across the Catawba River from western Mecklenburg County. Its population was 15,010 at the 2020 census. The city should not be confused with the Belmont neighborhood inside Charlotte.

Housing includes historic mill-era homes, newer subdivisions, townhomes, and some waterfront homes on Lake Wylie and the Catawba River. overview: Fort Mill is a town in York County, South Carolina, just south of the North Carolina line. Its population was 24,521 at the 2020 census. Some businesses and residents in Indian Land, in neighboring Lancaster County, share a Fort Mill mailing address, but the town boundary itself lies within York County.

Housing includes historic homes near downtown, large master-planned communities, newer subdivisions, and townhomes. The Anne Springs Close Greenway offers trails and nature programs, and Carowinds is nearby at the state line. I-77 and US 21 connect Fort Mill to Charlotte and Rock Hill. Fort Mill uses ZIP codes 29715 and 29708. Because Fort Mill is in South Carolina, property taxes, purchase contracts, and closing practices differ from North Carolina; see the SC buying note.
shopping: Shopping centers along US 21 and SC 160

faq.q: What state is Fort Mill in?
faq.a: South Carolina (York County).

faq.q: What ZIP codes are in Fort Mill?
faq.a: Fort Mill uses ZIP codes 29715 and 29708.

faq.q: Is buying in Fort Mill different from Charlotte?
faq.a: Yes. South Carolina has different property tax rules, contract forms, and closing practices; work with an SC-licensed agent and attorney.

cities.sc_buying_note: Buying in South Carolina differs from North Carolina in a few ways: SC owner-occupants must apply to the county for the 4% legal residence property-tax assessment ratio (otherwise property is generally assessed at 6%), SC uses different purchase contract forms than the NC Offer to Purchase and Contract (which includes a non-refundable due diligence fee paid to the seller), and closings commonly involve an SC-licensed attorney. Work with an agent licensed in South Carolina and consult an SC attorney for specifics.

overview: Indian Trail is a town in Union County, southeast of Charlotte. It has grown rapidly, from 1,942 residents in 1990 to 39,997 in 2020, due to its proximity to Charlotte and its appeal as a residential community for commuters.

Housing is mainly suburban single-family subdivisions and townhomes, many built since the 1990s, with some older homes and acreage. Shopping and services are concentrated along US 74 and Indian Trail Road. US 74 and the Monroe Expressway connect residents to Charlotte and Monroe. Indian Trail uses ZIP code 28079. Buyers should check whether a property is inside town limits.

overview: Waxhaw is an incorporated town in Union County, south of Charlotte. Its population was 20,534 at the 2020 census, more than double its 2010 population. The town's name comes from the Waxhaw people, who lived in the area.

Waxhaw's historic downtown, with its shops and restaurants, is a focal point for the community. Housing includes historic homes near downtown, master-planned communities, newer subdivisions, and some acreage. Cane Creek Park, a large Union County park with a lake, is to the southeast. NC 16 and NC 75 connect residents to Charlotte and Monroe. Waxhaw uses ZIP code 28173.

overview: Mooresville is a town in southwestern Iredell County, about 25 miles north of Charlotte. Its population was 50,193 at the 2020 census, making it the most populous municipality in Iredell County.

Mooresville is known as Race City USA for the many NASCAR teams and racing businesses based there, and it is home to the corporate headquarters of Lowe's. Housing includes lakefront homes, golf communities, newer subdivisions, and townhomes. Lake Norman State Park is nearby in Troutman, and I-77 connects Mooresville to Charlotte.
